extracted.intended_audience: TV viewers and fans who want a concise guide to sitcoms with new episodes or confirmed renewals in the 2025–2026 cycle
extracted.subtask_description: Compile a listicle of sitcoms that are currently in season, dropping new episodes soon, or officially renewed for the 2025–2026 cycle, with short at-a-glance entries for each show. Each entry should include distribution, timing, key cast, and essential production facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion criterion: current/new-season status
rubrics_metrics.description: List sitcoms that "have new episodes this year or confirmed new seasons in the 2025 to 2026 cycle."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Everything included should be either currently in season, dropping new episodes soon, or officially renewed and on the schedule (e.g., shows with new episodes in Oct 2025, Netflix drops in 2025, confirmed renewals for 2025–2026).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide at-a-glance essentials for each entry
rubrics_metrics.description: Each entry includes "the essentials you need at a glance, like where it streams, when new episodes arrive, who is in it, and how many seasons are out."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep entries concise but informative: platform, premiere/return timing, principal cast, and season count should be present for every show.

rubrics_metrics.name: State distribution and streaming details
rubrics_metrics.description: Note where the show airs and where it streams after broadcast (e.g., "streams on Paramount Plus after broadcast", "next day streaming on Hulu", "drops on Hulu all episodes at once").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include specifics about simulcasts, next-day availability, exclusive streaming platforms, and regional notes (e.g., Hulu, Paramount Plus, Netflix, Peacock, Apple TV Plus, Prime Video, Disney Plus).

rubrics_metrics.name: Give concrete release timing and schedule information
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify when new episodes or seasons arrive (exact premiere dates, month/year, or seasonal window) and release patterns (weekly, all-at-once, two-episode launch, back-to-back episodes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the list: precise dates (e.g., "September 15 2025"), monthly windows ("October 2025"), and patterns ("drop all ten episodes at once", "weekly release after two-episode premiere").

rubrics_metrics.name: List principal cast and creators
rubrics_metrics.description: Include main stars and, where relevant, creators/co-creators (e.g., "Quinta Brunson", "Justin Roiland and Mike McMahan", "Regina Hicks and Wanda Sykes serving as co creators").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Name the leading ensemble or notable voice actors and, when mentioned, highlight creators or showrunners to give context and name recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe the show's premise briefly
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a one- or two-sentence description of the show's setting or premise (e.g., "follows teachers at a Philadelphia public school", "centers on a couple sharing their upstate house with a chatty group of ghosts").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep synopses short and focused on the core hook so readers know what kind of sitcom it is (workplace, family, animated, sci-fi, mockumentary, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: State production format and style
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate production style: single camera, multi camera, mockumentary, documentary-style interviews, live audience feel, animated, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the production format to set audience expectations for tone and pacing (examples: "single camera mockumentary style", "multi camera format", "animated", "hospital mockumentary").

rubrics_metrics.name: Include runtime and typical episode length
rubrics_metrics.description: Note episode runtimes (e.g., "about half an hour", "22 minutes") so readers know the time commitment for each episode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where available, report the usual runtime (half hour vs 22 minutes) and mention if a show deviates from standard lengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report episode counts and season orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Mention recent season episode orders or typical season lengths (e.g., "mid teens to low twenties", "ten episodes", "12 episode drop", "around twenty two episodes").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include whether seasons arrive in parts, full-season drops, or split runs, and note if a season is labelled final or as a part number (e.g., "fifth and final season, known as Part Seven").

rubrics_metrics.name: Note filming location and production base
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide where the show is filmed or produced (e.g., Los Angeles, Vancouver, Montreal, Ireland, Atlanta, Oregon).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production locations are used repeatedly in entries; include them where stated to add production context (sometimes tied to tax incentives, local crews, or authentic setting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag renewal, final-season, or cancellation context
rubrics_metrics.description: State renewal status or whether a listed season is the final chapter (e.g., "renewed for another season", "confirmed the fifth and final season").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers expect clarity about a show's future — explicitly note renewals, multi-season pickups, announced finales, and sendoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include network scheduling and block context
rubrics_metrics.description: Mention where the show fits in a network's schedule or programming blocks (e.g., "airing on ABC’s fall schedule", "part of Fox’s comedy blocks", "NBC kept the series on Friday nights").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scheduling context helps readers anticipate when episodes air and understand network placement and promotion strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover both animated and live-action sitcoms and subgenres
rubrics_metrics.description: The list explicitly spans "long running animated staples to new network standouts and streaming hits," covering animated, workplace, family, sci-fi, and mockumentary sitcoms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be inclusive across subgenres and platforms; do not restrict the list to one style or distribution model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mention production company or studio credit
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the production company or studio associated with the series (e.g., "Warner Bros. Television", "20th Television Animation", "Bento Box Entertainment").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Studio credits add industry context and are listed for many shows; include them when provided.
